This file is the canonical substance store for Project Io's weekly sprint rhythm — every
sprint's goal, planned items, retro (landed/slipped/runtime/feedback) and free-form notes
(rulings, audit tables, amendments, risk paragraphs) that don't fit the fixed fields.
SPRINTS.md itself is now a thin header: intro prose, the Format template, and a regenerated
compact status table pointing here.
FIELDS per entry in `sprints`:
id           — sprint number/label as used in prose (e.g. '19', '26a', '22-24 preamble').
theme        — short human handle for the sprint (pair with id in prose, same rule as BL ids).
state        — one of: open, closed, proposed, superseded, gated, subsumed, retro-recorded, landed.
opened_date / closed_date — ISO dates where recorded in the source prose; null where the
entry never carries an explicit date (many 'proposed' entries were never opened).
goal         — the sprint's stated (or reconstructed, for retro-recorded entries) goal.
planned      — array of planned items/work, one string per item, as close to source phrasing
as practical.
retro        — object with landed/slipped/filed/runtime/feedback string fields where the
source entry carries a closed retro. Omitted for sprints with no retro yet.
risk         — the sprint's stated risk paragraph(s), where present.
done_when    — the sprint's stated done-when criterion, where present.
notes        — catch-all prose: rulings, audit tables (rendered as markdown), amendments,
'what this sprint deliberately does not carry' sections, sequencing notes. This is where
almost all of the original file's density lives for the larger/proposal-style entries.
The 'Sprints 26-33: The Fall' arc (proposed 2026-08-18) is captured as one parent entry
(id '26-33', the full audit/shape/rulings/adversarial-pass prose) plus one entry per named
D1-D4) — the two that actually opened (26a, 26b) carry their own opened_date and status-table
row; the rest stay 'proposed' pending Ben's pick, per the source.
`status_table` mirrors the source file's 'Where things stand' index — id/theme/state only,
for a quick scan; the full prose for every row lives in `sprints` above.
Landed items referenced by BL-id here are NOT re-described — see backlog.json (or the cold
archive once landed) for that item's own design/resolution prose. This file is about the
sprint as a unit of pacing and sequencing, not a duplicate backlog.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22, same convention as backlog.json): a sprint entry may carry
an `author` field naming who is running it (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only; nullable;
missing/null means unattributed (the default dev-sprint rhythm).

sprints.notes: Diagnosis before any work: 119 commits since the v0.1.0 tag and not one version cut, with CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] still reading "Nothing yet" — the changelog was not merely un-stamped, it was not accruing. Root cause (NR-103): the roadmap wrote done-definitions for exactly two versions, v0.1.0 and v1.0.0 — and those were the only two ever cut or scheduled. A theme with no done-definition has no test for finished, so it absorbs items indefinitely (v0.1.1 was the proof: its three theme legs shipped 2026-08-03, and 26 unrelated items were then retrofitted onto the same tag over the following week). Measurement overturned the stated cause four times: BL-338 wetland (story: relief commits displaced it; measured: refuted by rebuilding the audit at 802421c^ — identical census, wetland is a drainage feature and elevation had no vote in composition), BL-347 econ tick (story: an O(n log n) sort; measured: the sort was 3%, cost was std::map allocation in worlds with no stacks), BL-346 estimator (story: BL-079's reflex reads an inflated number; measured: retracted — that function reads realised credit, real site was the pre-build estimator), pan "lag" (story: needs a 200ms input delay; measured: panning costs nothing, static and panning measured identically — it was 157k vertices at whole-grid zoom). A green gate can lie: logistics_reach_harness failed three assertions from byte-identical sources — a conflict-heavy merge left ninja holding a stale object that touch would not dislodge. Standing lesson: --clean-first before cutting after a messy merge, and if a harness fails suspiciously, build the same commit in a throwaway worktree before believing it. sprints.notes: Where the method held: by not doing the thing — Sprint 6's worst cost was worktree agents branching from a moved base (36 conflicts to integrate one commit); this sprint's three items were one dependency chain across ~2 files each, so built sequentially in the main session, stated as a call rather than defaulted into. This item is why BL-315's own ruling has been waiting: army/mercenary/pirate are three derived readings of one company, the reading is derived never authored; army and mercenary have paths to being read, pirate has NO mechanic at all — taking a convoy is exactly that act. SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-310) — capture, with destruction as the fallback. Cargo leaves the source pool at dispatch, so both answers conserve. On interception the cargo credits the interceptor's (corp, body) pool at the interception body; where it cannot be credited it is destroyed instead, and the outcome says which — an interceptor with no market access holds goods it cannot sell, a legitimate outcome, NOT special-cased away. What decided it: destroy-only pays the interceptor zero, so BL-450's scored-utility stance layer would correctly never rank an interception — interdiction would ship as a capability only the player ever uses, the same unreachable-capability defect this sprint exists to fix. Capture gives the scorer a number, and earns BL-315's third derived reading: a company that takes cargo reads as a pirate, one that only burns it reads as a saboteur. Harness's load-bearing row: captured quantity == quantity credited exactly, with the destroyed-fallback path asserting zero credited and zero minted. Not a battle by default — a convoy is cargo, not a force, the first cut resolves interception as an OUTCOME; escort (a unit assigned to a convoy, turning interception into a real resolve_campaign_battle call) is the obvious follow-on, deliberately out because it needs BL-315's engagement machinery SHIPPED not merely built. SETTLED 2026-08-17 (Ben, on NR-312): 25a runs next, sequence is 25a → 21 → 23 → 25b — interdiction, the payoff this sprint was rescoped to carry, is now three sprints out; the alternative (opening Sprint 23 stance first as shortest path) was on the table, Ben chose the substrate instead, the reading that leaves 25b with fewer unknowns when it arrives. sprints.retro:
CLOSED 2026-08-21 having overshot its own done_when by five items. The goal — provinces grown from settlement and stopped by terrain — was met by BL-515 before this session opened. What followed was Ben's tile/province brief of the same day, and it turned out to be one arc rather than a follow-on: the axis split, the texturing it unblocked, water kinds, the ceiling ruling, and the click injection that exists so a non-interactive agent can check any of it.

WHAT THE SPRINT ACTUALLY PROVED, and it is a method claim rather than a feature one:

1. THE METHOD NOTE HELD A SECOND TIME. The sprint's own note says every ruling that stuck was made against a RENDER, not a spec. BL-519 repeated it in a form nobody had budgeted for: the forest-on-rock threshold was set at the value the design implied (moisture >= 0.55), MEASURED, and found to fire zero times — because the biome table only ever draws rocky ground in the dry and middling columns, so wet rock does not exist for the branch to find. The item's headline case would have shipped INERT and looked implemented. Measuring the new behaviour, not just the regression, is what caught it (NR-446).

2. A REFACTOR CAN BE MADE FALSIFIABLE, and it is worth the structure. BL-519 was 522 references across ~110 files. It was landable in one pass because Pass 4a's RNG consumption was held identical draw-for-draw and both new passes consume no stream at all — so the claim 'nothing drifted' could be tested rather than asserted. The 120-seed earthlike census came back BIT-IDENTICAL, and that one measurement is what made every other moved number attributable. Carry this: when a refactor touches a seeded pipeline, the cheap thing is to keep the stream fixed and let a census prove it.

3. THE CEILING RULING GENERALISED IMMEDIATELY. NR-438's shape — a stated number becomes a PREFERENCE, a real bound is ASSERTED, and the over-share is REPORTED because 'rare' was never defined — was reused within hours by BL-516's sea provinces, which hit exactly the same wall at 82 against 'say 80' (NR-460). A ruling that produces a reusable discipline is worth more than one that produces a number.

4. THE FAN-OUT COST AN HOUR, and the cause is filed (NR-459). Three agents ran concurrently; all three got worktrees at the SESSION's base rather than at HEAD. One fast-forwarded itself, one did not and built an entire item against the enum BL-519 had just deleted. The port was cheap only because that agent had routed every water test through one choke-point predicate. Two agents also independently minted the same review ids, because NEEDS_REVIEW.json has no next_id.js. Both are process fixes, not judgement failures.

WHAT IS OWED, and it is the honest weakness of the whole arc: NOTHING WAS RENDERED. Four of the six items have a UI half, and the session ran in a container that cannot build the GUI. Everything is compile-clean against real ImGui headers and arithmetically checked; none of it has been seen. No golden was blessed, because blessing an unseen frame pins whatever got built. For a sprint whose own method note is 'build it, look at it, then rule', ending without the looking is the thing to fix — and BL-521, built this same session, is what makes the looking cheap next time.

CARRIED FORWARD: BL-518 (the Era -1 sim redrawing borders as its wars resolve) is the last clause of Ben's brief and is still design-owed with three undecided questions. BL-514 (blend all tiles) stays HELD, and BL-520 has now given it a second reason to be decided — texture and the blend are in direct tension.

sprints.retro:
**All three lanes merged and green; one lane's CONCLUSION was withdrawn after the merge, and that is the sprint's finding.**

What landed: BL-542's nation scorer (60/60, the first use of the 2026-08-18 grant), BL-546's migration of reputation onto the sentiment substrate with BL-391 dissolved through it (66 PASS, two save formats moved), and Sprint 28 lane A's verb-competition instrumentation (4/4). Re-verified on the integrated tree rather than on branches: nine harnesses green, zero ASan/UBSan diagnostics, warning-clean at -Wall -Wextra.

**Two lane reports did not survive verification, and neither would have been caught by reading.** A claimed layout-sensitive determinism violation in spectate does not reproduce on four clean trees, and the lane's own probe re-run moves neither hash — the likely cause, a stale object left in a rebuilt archive, bit a sibling lane in the same run and it said so. Filing it as reported would have put a false violation into the one invariant the project cannot compromise on. And a ceiling-vs-floor statistic folded its subject's WINNING scores into the ceiling, conditioning it on the outcome it explained; harmless here by luck, and fixed to the honest form.

**The bigger one came from the adversarial pass, and it invalidated the sprint's headline.** Sprint 28's finding — that Campaign's score ceiling sits below the winner's floor on exactly the silent worlds — was a two-case coincidence. At n=32 only 3 of 17 silent seeds are disjoint and 14 overlap, worst by 142 points; the diagnosis that the defect is the score LEVEL is unsupported (seed 8 clears 27,452 and fights 676 battles, seed 30 clears 2,338,095 and fights zero); and zero-war is the MODAL outcome at 53%, not a 25% pathology. What survives is the fork's answer, which is a statement about the decision rule rather than about a world: wherever a world fights nothing, Campaign clears its threshold and loses the argmax on every round.

**And underneath all of it, the instrument was measuring a sim the game does not run** — six divergences from the app's own invocation, one of which gates a whole verb out of the contest. That belongs to BL-462, which has owned it since 2026-08-18 and which this session initially duplicated as BL-554 by not searching the backlog first (NR-556).

**The method lesson, and it is N1's repeated with the stakes raised.** N1 taught that an author's own harness passes; N2 briefed every lane to mutation-test its own rows and every lane did, catching two of its own false greens before reporting. That worked. What it did not catch is the class above it: a green harness measuring the wrong fixture, and a true measurement generalised from n=2. Mutation testing proves a row has teeth against the code; it says nothing about whether the FIXTURE is the subject, or whether the SAMPLE supports the claim. Both need a different check, and the adversarial pass is what supplied it.

**Owed out of N2:** every spine still has no caller. BL-538 is the join, and it opens N3.

**POSTSCRIPT, same day.** BL-462 was fixed and the era re-measured, which supersedes both readings above. The real Era -1: **11 of 32 worlds fight nothing (34%)**, BL-384's premise is dead (2,503 battles produce 1,789 conquests), the fork answer survives on all 11 silent worlds, and **nothing separates** silent from fighting — 32 of 32 seeds overlap on the statistic that had looked decisive, and six candidate separators have now been tested and refuted. The one universal: Settle takes 83–100% of the rounds Campaign loses on every world. So three passes were needed to get one trustworthy number, and the sequence — a finding, a sample that refuted it, a fixture that refuted the sample — is the sprint's real record.

sprints.theme: The shell stops fighting the map
sprints.goal:
BATCH DELIVERY over Ben's 2026-08-24 UI list (BL-596..BL-604), slotted between Sprint 17 and Sprint 18 because 17 is running as the economy sprint in another session and this is the UI work in the same slot. Opened earlier the same day under the placeholder lane id U1 and re-slotted here on Ben's instruction; nothing else about it changed.

WHY A BATCH AND NOT NINE ITEMS. Ben: 'let's try to go with batch deliver to fix aspects of the UI all together.' The list is not nine independent tweaks, and treating it as nine would guarantee the incoherence it is meant to remove. Five of the nine are ONE design - the lens system and the selection grain rebuilt around STRUCTURES rather than tiles, with the chrome that serves them collected into one home - and every one of the seven remaining items lands in body_surface_canvas.cpp, overlay.cpp or both. Delivered serially, each would re-open the same two files, re-bless the same captures, and settle the same questions differently. Delivered as a batch they clear step 4 together, take ONE cross-slice review pass, and re-bless once.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE. BL-599 and BL-600 landed on the day the sprint opened (27d0aed8): the right chrome column now meets the top, right and bottom screen edges, and the 8px strip of live ocean between the Selection band and the minimap is gone. sprints.retro:
CLOSED 2026-08-24, GOAL MET. All nine items complete: BL-599/BL-600 the day the sprint opened, then four parallel slices and one main-session wave. Final sweep 93 verify scripts, 4 failures, and all four fail on a PRE-SPRINT build too (NR-606). Goldens re-blessed at the close, once, as planned.

WHAT THE BATCH BOUGHT. Six of the seven waved items touch body_surface_canvas.cpp or overlay.cpp. Run serially each would have re-opened those files, re-blessed the same captures and answered the same questions separately - and the answers really did depend on each other: A1 and B both retired an overlay_mode value and their strip edits had to be UNIONED at the merge, and A2's plate removal and A1's country-tint removal were the same three lines of one function. Five conflicted files, all resolvable because each slice owned a coherent SUBJECT rather than a file.

THE METHOD LESSON, three independent instances in one sprint: A CHECK THAT HARD-CODES A SCREEN COORDINATE IS A CHECK WITH A SHELF LIFE. built_tile_render.lua was framing open ocean and passing green (found by A2, pre-existing). border_band.lua passed in its author's worktree and failed the moment four slices merged, because its press point was measured by eye against one build. lens_structure_pivot.lua failed its own control twice - first pressing a tile with a marker on it, then caching a screen point before a press that OPENED A LEDGER and narrowed the canvas under it. Every one was a coordinate that outlived the world it was measured in. The fix each time was to resolve from the world at use, and it is now written into three scripts.

WHAT WAS FOUND THAT NOBODY WENT LOOKING FOR. Four doc fictions: LENSES.md's rung table claims Circumplanetary/Solar surfaces for Scarcity, Reach and Supply-routes that were never built (Production's retired with its lens), and its routing table's 'a building under the Corporation lens resolves through to its corporation' had been stated since 2026-06-15 and never implemented - discovered because BL-603's check asserted the DOCUMENTED behaviour and it failed. Two landed-item surprises: BL-086's ambient opportunity read was the Opportunity lens itself and retires with it (NR-603), and BL-514 was not held-awaiting-Ben as its prose says - it landed 2026-08-22 and is what made the land smear Ben objected to. And the first full sweep anyone has run found four rotten checks, one of which (battle_card) had never executed at all.

WHAT BEN'S ANSWERS CHANGED.
